title: Xenophon's Oeconomicus I-VI: Socrates on wealth as use, mastery of desires, and the noble life of husbandry
summary: Socrates tells Critobulus that wealth is only what one knows how to use well, and that the true masters of men are unseen vices like idleness, luxury and lust. He then recommends learning from those who succeed, praises husbandry as a school of justice, bravery and friendship, and sets out to find the truly "beautiful and good" man.

principles.text: Wealth is only what benefits you; the same thing is wealth or not depending on whether you know how to use it.
principles.quote: The same things, in fact, are wealth or not wealth, according as a man knows or does not know the use to make of them.

principles.text: Money misused to the harm of body and soul is not wealth at all; better banished than counted as wealth.
principles.quote: Let money then, Critobulus, if a man does not know how to use it aright--let money, I say, be banished to the remote corners of the earth rather than be reckoned as wealth.

principles.text: Friends are true wealth if you know how to use them well, more than cattle.
principles.quote: If a man knows how to use his friends so as to be benefited by them, what of these?

principles.text: The real tyrants are inner vices like idleness, luxury and lust; we must wage ceaseless war on them for freedom's sake.
principles.quote: Ah! Critobulus, against these must we wage ceaseless war, for very freedom's sake, no less than if they were armed warriors endeavouring to make us their slaves.

principles.text: Contentment with little is riches; a man's wants set his true wealth, so Socrates calls himself rich and the wealthy Critobulus poor.
principles.quote: My property is amply sufficient to meet my wants, whereas you, considering the parade you are fenced about with, and the reputation you must needs live up to, would be barely well off

principles.text: Honestly admit what you do not know and send the learner to those who know better; careful attention is rewarded and carelessness punished.
principles.quote: Those who carried on their affairs in a haphazard manner I saw were punished by their losses; whilst those who kept their wits upon the stretch and paid attention I soon perceived to be rewarded
